warnings: No played matches have been performed.
Source briefs are a first pass; unresolved passage verification remains labelled.
Hunter approved WU Penelope and explicitly selected actual sacrifice for Iphigenia. Slot 015 now remains UB; its proposed rate still needs testing.

The seven Studio notes remain open until actual implementation is verified.
Candidate references need a production refresh before integration.

cards.name: The Olive-Wood Test
cards.rules: Target permanent you control gains indestructible until end of turn. If it's legendary, scry 1.
cards.story: Book XXIII / Penelope's test turns on the secret that their marriage bed was built around a living olive trunk and cannot simply be moved.
cards.credit: Art: “Ulysses and Penelope” · Francesco Primaticcio · Wildenstein Collection, New York · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XXIII / the immovable marriage bed proves Odysseus's identity to Penelope.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Only the couple knows how the rooted bed was made, so knowledge of its immovability becomes the decisive recognition test.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A clean common relationship card for Penelope and the legendary Olive-Wood Bed: it literally makes a permanent impossible to move or destroy for the turn.

cards.name: Keep the Long Watch
cards.rules: Constellation — Whenever an enchantment you control enters, put a quest counter on Keep the Long Watch and create a 1/1 white Human Citizen creature token. This ability triggers only once each turn. Then if Keep the Long Watch has three or more quest counters on it, sacrifice it. When you do, you gain 3 life.

cards.flavorStoryElement: The challenge rewards simply doing the work of the turn—attacking, crewing or otherwise tapping creatures—until the household has endured long enough to grow.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The current long-watch flavour is retained while Household Restored’s enchantment-to-Citizen engine is folded into the progression challenge: each new enchantment marks time, adds someone to the functioning household, and the third watch completes the ordeal.

cards.name: Argos, Who Waited

cards.flavorStoryElement: The first creature in Ithaca to recognise Odysseus without proof is his dying dog Argos.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Vigilance captures faithful waiting; the death trigger recovers a small legendary permanent, making Argos a literal bridge back to a remembered person or object. Existing Athena art must be replaced.

cards.name: Telemachus Calls the Assembly
cards.rules: Create two 1/1 white Human Citizen creature tokens. If you control a legendary creature, tap up to one target creature an opponent controls and put a stun counter on it.

cards.flavorStoryElement: Telemachus's coming of age first becomes public when he claims the right to speak and asks the community to witness what is happening in his house.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The assembly now has an efficient board presence at three mana. Citizens physically gather, while a legendary speaker such as Telemachus can publicly check one opposing creature with a stun counter. The art is moved from a generic Pnyx view to a direct Telemachus painting.

cards.name: Steer by the Great Bear

cards.flavorStoryElement: A fixed star pattern becomes practical orientation when no coastline is available.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Scry reads the sky; untapping a Vehicle turns that knowledge into renewed movement. The inland-oar art must be replaced.

cards.name: Loyal Householder
cards.rules: Survival — At the beginning of your second main phase, if Loyal Householder is tapped, untap another target permanent you control.
cards.story: Ithaca / ordinary household labor and endurance during Odysseus’s long absence.

cards.flavorStoryElement: Ordinary Ithacan household life continuing under strain while Odysseus is absent.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: Survival rewards a worker who has been active, then restores another permanent, returning this slot from an invented late-prophecy interpreter to grounded Ithacan household connective tissue.

cards.name: Feign Madness

cards.flavorStoryElement: Odysseus pretends madness to evade the summons to Troy, making himself appear incapable of command.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A one-mana Dive Down-style protection spell with a real disguise cost: the creature survives as a harmless 0/4 with hexproof but loses all abilities. The ability loss can also be exploited deliberately.

cards.rules: Foretell {1}{U}. Tap target creature. It doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step. Draw a card.

cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: Foretell makes the storm impending; tapping a creature and keeping it from untapping makes the storm physically stop forward motion.

As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a nontoken creature.
Tap all creatures your opponents control. Draw two cards.
cards.story: At Aulis, Calchas interprets the snake-and-sparrows omen as a sign that Troy will fall only after a long war.
cards.credit: Art: Roman fresco, House of the Tragic Poet · MANN · photo Jebulon
cards.changeStatus: story-retheme-v2 · art-review · flavor-redesign-v1 · art-sweep-v1 · art-p1-named-v1 · omen-boardwipe-recast-v1 · reference-qa-v1 · template-cleanup-v1 · studio-notes-pass-20260921

cards.name: Singer at the Hearth

cards.flavorStoryElement: The singer turns the top of the library into a small repertoire of actions and enchantments, mechanically locating stories in performance rather than archives.
